messages.subject: Problem with Math Expression changed by user
messages.subject_clean: Problem with Math Expression changed by user
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I hope to create a friendly-user shiny interface.

Im wondering whether shiny has a widget (let name it "func") which can allow user input any equation (example: -x^2). and it can be passed to

f<-function(x){(input$func)}  and the result will be calculated as a value when user input x value.

i hav tried using textInput("func",.....) then  f<-function(x){ input$func } but it doesn't work.

Thank you.

messages.subject: shiny-server on Raspberry Pi/Raspian crashing upon launch
messages.subject_clean: shiny-server on Raspberry Pi/Raspian crashing upon launch
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've just finished building shiny-server from source successfully on my
Raspberry Pi running Raspian Linux (Linux My-Berry-01 4.0.9-v7+ #807 SMP
PREEMPT Fri Jul 24 15:21:02 BST 2015 armv7l GNU/Linux), but when trying to
launch 'shiny-server' it immediately crashes with a flood of error messages
(no log files are being written).

My '*shiny-server.conf*' reads

run_as shiny;

socket_dir /var/run/shiny-server;
access_log /var/log/shiny-server/access.log tiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
 server_name My-Berry-01;
 listen 3838;

 template_dir /usr/local/etc/shiny-server/templates;
 r_path /usr/local/bin/R;

 ## Define a location at the base URL
 location / {
 # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
 site_dir /data/shiny/base;

 # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
 log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

 # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
 # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
 directory_index on;
 }

 ## Run this location in 'app_dir' mode, which will host a single Shiny
 location /apps {
 app_dir /data/shiny/apps;
 } # apps
} # server

Logging the output of 'shiny-server' results in (see below).

Any hint as what is causing this, or how to tackle this one would be more
than appreciated! :)

-- Sil68

messages.body_plain:
On Monday, July 27, 2015 at 1:17:47 AM UTC-5, Amber James wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I am trying to expand my application for my company a bit and I cannot seem to find any articles online that would assist me in this. I am attempting to use the DT library range selector but I want to use it in a non-conventional sense.
>
> I am currently using the DT library for its row selection features. The user will essentially choose a column(s) and, from that, the DT is auto generated with only unique values from the column(s) selected. When someone wants to choose a unique value to plot on the graph they simply click the value and the plot is generated the N values that are currently under the rows_selected category.
>
> My question is this, is there a way, if the user utilizes the range selection in association with DT filtering, that I can retrieve the selected ranged data. Ultimately, I want to give the user the option of choosing that range as a plotted value.
>

Amber, you mentioned selecting columns, but you say that selected DT, I guess you mean data.tables, for row selection features. I don't know about selecting columns, but if you want to select rows, you can use two selectInput() statements, one for the start of your range and the other for the end of your range and then reference the respective index values. That works for rows, I don't see why it won't work for columns. I'm not exactly an ace programmer though.

shinyUI(fluidPage(

 titlePanel("stockVis"),

      textInput("symb", "Symbol", "SPY"),

      dateRangeInput("dates",

        start = "2013-01-01",

      actionButton("get", "Get Stock"),

        value = FALSE),

      checkboxInput("adjust",
        "Adjust prices for inflation", value = FALSE)
    ),

    mainPanel(plotOutput("plot"))
  )
))

# server.R

library(quantmod)
source("helpers.R")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- getSymbols(input$symb, src = "yahoo",
      from = input$dates[1],
      to = input$dates[2],
      auto.assign = FALSE)

    chartSeries(data, theme = chartTheme("white"),
      type = "line", log.scale = input$log, TA = NULL)
  })

})

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:4430

Error : Failed to download file. Error message:
unsupported URL scheme

1. Explicitly pass method= via the getSymbols call (or via setDefaults)
2. Install downloader, which may be able to automagically determine a method
3. Set the download.file.method global option

Thank you very much.
Ted

messages.body_plain:
I might not offer the full solution. But I wanted to make a comment, that I had an issue when working with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, when I used a method in my code that only worked for Windows environment, like downloading files using a certain function. Shinyapps.io however runs in a Linux (or non-Windows) environment, so my code failed. When I re-wrote my method to work for Macs/Linux, it worked ok (now it wouldn't run locally, but I used it as a separate version strictly for Shinyapps.io).

Maybe that doesn't help much, but just keep that in mind, when writing code for Shinyapps.io

Good luck.

messages.subject_clean: Select DT rows when input IDs are unknown
messages.body_plain:
You are supposed to use UI functions (e.g. dataTableOutput()) inside
renderUI(). I don't understand what it means to use renderDataTable()
in renderUI(). renderDataTable() is supposed to be assigned to
output$tableId (where tableId may be dt1, dt2, dt3 in your case).

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors
messages.subject_clean: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors
messages.body_plain:
Labels are for users to read and choose from, and values are for app
authors (e.g. you). Users probably don't care about values, and
authors don't care about labels. It is totally your choice to use
unique values or not. If you want to know exactly which choice the
user selected, you have to use unique values.

Regards,
Yihui

Thank you so much for clarifying and pointing me into the right direction. The example I showed was influenced by another problem I had earlier and which was answered here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31749339/reactivity-of-dynamic-number-of-ui-elements

I managed to solve both problems with the following solution:

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput("tabs")
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$tabs <- renderUI({
      tables <- lapply( list("dt1", "dt2", "dt3"), function(x){

        local({
          output[[x]] <- renderDataTable( DT::datatable( data.frame("data") ) )
        })
        observeEvent({
          input[[paste( x, "rows_selected", sep="_" )]]
        },{
          print( paste( x, ":", input[[paste( x, "rows_selected", sep="_" )]] ) )
        })
        dataTableOutput( x )
      })
      tagList(tables)
    })
  }
)

If no one sees another problem with this code, for completeness sake I'd answer both questions on SO accordingly.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)
messages.subject_clean: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)
messages.body_plain:
Suppose I have a function like this in an R package:

launch_my_app(X) {
  Y <- preprocess(X)   # where preprocess does a bunch of computations that I'd like to avoid doing inside of the Shiny app
  shiny::runApp(...)   # where ...  are the appropriate arguments to runApp
}

where I'd the app to then use the object Y (e.g. do stuff to Y in server.R, etc.).

Of course, with Shiny's scoping rules this won't work, as Y will not be accessible. The only solution I've found is to assign Y to the user's global environment (e.g. using something like assign("Y", preprocess(X), inherits = TRUE)), in which case it works great. But this is part of an R package and so I'd like to avoid assignments to the global environment like this.

Am I missing an easy way to make this work or, if not, does anyone have any clever ideas?

messages.body_plain:
Add the shiny::runApp() call to your server.R (I would place it at the end of the file). Then, your function becomes

launch_my_app(X) {
 Y <- preprocess(X)
 source(PATH_TO_SERVER.R)
}

Would this work?

Ben

> Suppose I have a function like this in an R package:
>
> launch_my_app(X) {
>   Y <- preprocess(X)   # where preprocess does a bunch of computations that I'd like to avoid doing inside of the Shiny app

> }
>

That's exactly what I was going to look for. reactiveValues in global.R means that all of the user sessions are sharing the same copies of the variables and triggering each others' reactivity. Sometimes that is actually what you want, but not often!

Glad you were able to figure it out!

> As an update, I pulled the old version of my application and added my updates to that. I made my changes 1 by 1 to check the run time issues. Then, finally, I found the supposed little bugger. The issue seems to have stemmed from my global class. When I was performing code clean up I decided to put my reactiveValues into the global.R file so that the server only contained observe and observeEvent functions. Once I moved this back to the server itself the issues went away. HUZZAH!

messages.subject: value of dynamically generated textInput widget oscillates depending on typing speed
messages.subject_clean: value of dynamically generated textInput widget oscillates depending on typing speed
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I have an application with 0 or more textInputs, depending on user's actions.  I create them dynamically, and trap their values inside the server context.  When I re-generate the UI, I re-populate the textInput values from my trapped copies, since their their number may have changed for other reasons.

Ideally the user should be able to alter the text in the UI, and application should respect each alteration.  But apparently when typing at just the right rate, it is possible to drive the system into an unstable state where the text displayed alternates between the current and former input.  In some cases, the system stabilizes on one value.  The problem is more evident when more inputs are present.

Minimal example follows, with one hard-coded input.  Is it possible to trap or avoid this condition?

Thanks,

Tim

library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  server = function(input, output) {
    value <- ""
    output$ui <- renderUI({
      value <<- input$txt_0
      textInput("txt_0", "text", value)
    })
  },
  ui = fluidPage( fluidRow( column( 10, uiOutput("ui"))))
)

Ed

I'm having trouble creating a dynamic number of tabs in our shiny application. I want the end product to look like this

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-EOiWuWD_l3w/VcUPtxydQZI/AAAAAAAAABI/7bBPGPeOg-I/s1600/modeltabs.PNG>

This is also complicated by the fact that this app uses persistent data storage – if the user made and saved 5 tabs the first time they used the app, I want those same 5 tabs to appear when they use the app the next time. We already have a method of persistent data storage working (no need to worry about that right now), but I cannot figure out a way to generate tabs based on previously saved data.

I’ve tried creating tabs dynamically with do.call, and I am able to generate a variable number of tabs. However, populating each of those tabPanels with uniquely named textInputs has proved to be the challenge. And even then, interacting with those textInputs in order to save the data has given me the most trouble.

Is there a way to implement this kind of feature in a shiny app?

Thank you,

Ryan

Hi I am trying to creating a simple weather display, which will change the infobox color based on the temperature. The color value is correct as it displays correctly, but the color parameter will not recognize the color. I reports Error in validateColor(color) : Invalid color:
. Valid colors are: red, yellow, aqua, blue, light-blue, green, navy, teal, olive, lime, orange, fuchsia, purple, maroon, black. In addition: Warning message: In if (color %in% validColors) { : the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used The code is shown below with the critical lines highlighted. Any help would be appreciated Rick library(shiny) library(shinydashboard) library(RWeather) getColor <- function(station) { t <- as.numeric(getWeatherFromNOAA(station_id = station, message = FALSE)$temp_c) if(t > 30) {return('red')} else if (t < 5) {return('blue')} else return('yellow') } header <- dashboardHeader(title = 'Current weather') sidebar <- dashboardSidebar() boxCity <- box(selectInput('station', 'City:', choices = c('Atlanta' = 'KATL', 'Chicago' = 'KORD', 'Fairbanks' = 'PAFA', 'New York' = 'KJFK', 'Phoenix' ='KPHX'), selected = 'KATL')) boxCondition <- box(title = 'Current conditions: ', textOutput('condition'), background = 'blue') valueBoxC <- valueBox(textOutput('color'), width=3, subtitle = 'C', color= textOutput('color')) valueBoxF <- valueBox(textOutput('F'), width=3, subtitle = "F") boxTime <- box(textOutput('time')) row1 <- fluidRow(boxCity) row2 <- fluidRow(boxCondition, boxTime) row3 <- fluidRow(valueBoxC, valueBoxF) body <- dashboardBody(row1,row2,row3) ui <- dashboardPage(header,sidebar,body) server <- function(input, output) { output$text <- renderText({paste(input$station, ' weather watch')}) output$condition <- renderText({getWeatherFromNOAA(station_id = input$station, message = FALSE)$condition}) output$time <- renderText({getWeatherFromNOAA(station_id = input$station, message = FALSE)$observation_time}) output$F <- renderText({getWeatherFromNOAA(station_id = input$station, message = FALSE)$temp_f}) output$C <- renderText({getWeatherFromNOAA(station_id = input$station, message = FALSE)$temp_c}) output$color <- renderText({getColor(input$station)}) } shinyApp(ui, server)

Yes, the current development version (0.1.x) of DT always returns
numeric indices. It is a little annoying that it returns different
things depending on whether you use client-side or server-side
processing (moreover, when using server-side processing, you had to
make sure the first column is the row names).

rownames(data)[input$tableId_rows_selected]. Does that make sense?

messages.subject: valueBox linked to a menuItem with href
messages.subject_clean: valueBox linked to a menuItem with href
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a shinydashboard I've created and here what I would like to achieve : when the user has clicked on the menuItem "menu1", in the main part of the dashboard, there is a valueBox ("box1" for instance), and I would like that when the user clicks on this valueBox, it goes to the content of the menuItem "menu2" (as if the user had clicked on the menuItem "menu2").

I've seen the "href" parameter for "valueBox" elements and it seems to work perfectly well if I use an external link (such as "www.google.fr/ <http://www.google.fr/>" for instance) but when I tried to use an internal link from the app itself, it doesn't work as expected...

Here is the example code I used :

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

shinyUI <- dashboardPage(

  dashboardHeader(title="Test"),

  dashboardSidebar(

sidebarMenu(
             menuItem("Menu 1", tabName = "menu1", icon = icon("dashboard")),
     menuItem("Exemples", tabName = "menu2", icon = icon("gears")),
             menuItem("Contre-exemples", tabName = "menu3", icon = icon("gears"))
)
   ),
   dashboardBody(

    tabItems(

           tabItem(tabName = "menu1",

fluidRow(
column(width = 5,
valueBox(12, "exemples", color = "aqua", icon = icon("users"), href = "#shiny-tab-menu2", width = NULL)
),
column(width = 5,
valueBox(25, "contre-exemples", color = "maroon", icon = icon("users"), href = "#shiny-tab-menu3", width = NULL)
)
)
  ),

  tabItem(tabName = "menu2",

fluidRow(
  column(width = 5,
valueBox(12, "exemples", color = "aqua", icon = icon("users"), width = NULL)
  )
)
),
tabItem(tabName = "menu3",

fluidRow(
  column(width = 5,
valueBox(25, "contre-exemples", color = "maroon", icon = icon("users"), width = NULL)
  )
)
)
)

  )

)

And here what's happening for instance :

When I launch (in local) the app, I have the following adress in my navbar : http://127.0.0.1:4825/ , and I see the content of my menuItem "menu1" (by default).
Then, I click on the valueBox "box1" and nothing seems to change on the app : I still see the content of my menuItem "menu1" (instead of the content of "menu2") BUT in the navbar I have the following adresse : http://127.0.0.1:4825/#shiny-tab-menu2.
Then when I click directly on the menuItem "menu2", its content displays correctly, and after that, when I click on the menuItem "menu1", its content displays correctly too, eventhough I now still have http://127.0.0.1:4825/#shiny-tab-menu2 on my navbar.

> So I was wondering why the shinydashboard has this behavior and how to specify an internal href in order to link a valueBox to a menuItem ?

Don't hesitate to ask me if my description is not clear enough.
Thank you in advance for your help !

Best regards.

messages.subject: Warning in run(timeoutMs) # no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
messages.subject_clean: Warning in run(timeoutMs) # no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
messages.body_plain:
The following server.R code generates the warning when run locally on OS X:

Warning in run(timeoutMs) :
    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

When run on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> it appears to kill the process after the first (successful?) rendering. Perhaps what generates this strange warning has a darker side-effect there.

The problem line is:
    rgg <- projectRaster(rgg, rgg.proj) # this line generates the warning

No warnings are generated when run as a code snippet.

library(shiny)
library(sp)
library(raster)
library(rgdal)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    depth <- as.numeric(input$depth)
    filepath <- 'data4jerry'
    filename <- paste(filepath,"/temp",sprintf("%03d", depth),"day00.dat",sep='')
    d <- read.table(filename,na.strings='-99.0000',dec='.')$V1
    d[which(d==-98)] <- NA    # it appears both -99 and -98 are missing values
    nx = 1501
    ny = 421

    d2 <- matrix(d,nrow=ny,ncol=nx,byrow=TRUE)
    d3 <- d2[nrow(d2):1,] # flip to match rendering order

#    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:3573")
#    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:5638")
    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:4326")
    EPSGproj = CRS(input$proj)
    lon = -30. + (1:nx-1)/60.
    lat = 62. + (1:ny-1)/60.
    rgg = raster(d3,xmn=min(lon),xmx=max(lon),ymn=min(lat),ymx=max(lat),
                 crs="+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84")

    # this projectRaster section generates a warning when run locally
    #  Warning in run(timeoutMs) :
    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
    # and appears to kill the app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> after the 1st rendering.
    rgg.proj <- projectExtent(rgg, crs = EPSGproj)  # this line executes without warning
    rgg <- projectRaster(rgg, rgg.proj) # this line generates the warning

    ice<-c('#2C537E','#346498','#3D74B1','#6797CB','#7AB2D2','#8DCDD8','#19FFCC','#65FF66','#B2FF33','#FFFF00','#FFC000','#FF8000','#FF4040','#D00000','#A00000')
    brks <- seq(-2,13)
    arg <- list(at=brks[seq(1,length(brks),2)], labels=brks[seq(1,length(brks),2)])
    plot(rgg,col=ice,breaks=brks,lab.breaks=brks,
        # xlim=c(min(lon),max(lon)),ylim=c(min(lat),max(lat)),
         cex.axis=1.25,cex.lab=1.25,axis.args=arg #,
        #main=paste(input$depth,"m,",strsplit(input$proj,"=")[[1]][2])
        )
    contour(rgg,add=TRUE,labcex=1.25)
    })

})

Any hints?
Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Put the lapply(1:cnum(), ...) call inside of observe():

observe({
  lapply(1:cnum(), function(i) {

    output[[paste(paste("c",i,sep=""),"select",sep="")]] <- renderUI({
      assign(paste("comp",i,sep=""), tryCatch(setNames("test1","Test1"),
                                              error = function(e) setNames("none","None Found")))
      selectInput(paste(paste("c",i,sep=""),"ticker",sep=""), paste("Component",i,sep=" "), get(paste("comp",i,sep="")))
    })
  })

})
As an aside, instead of paste(paste("c",i,sep=""),"select",sep="") you could do any of the following:

paste("c", i, "select", sep = "")
paste0("c", i ,"select")
sprintf("c%dselect", i)

messages.subject: Is there (could there be) a reactive boolean to indicate that the UI has finished rendering?

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm using Dean Attali's nifty shinyjs package, but I have run across an issue when using enable/disable of dynamic elements.

I'm not the first one to come across this; great writeup of the issue here:

https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/issues/25

To highlight one of the questions raised there, I was just wondering if there is (or if there could be) a reactive available that indicates when the html has finished rendering?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.body_plain:
I am trying to create a Shiny application wherein the user inputs a text string to search on twitter along with the option to choose the number of tweets to fetch, the language of the tweets and the ability to download the tweets in a csv file. I want the output to be a table of the last 5 tweets and a word cloud of the tweets fetched. I was able to get the tweets, display the last 5 tweets but I am not able to download the tweets and get the correct word cloud output using the following code:
library(shiny)
library(twitteR)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Tweets hunter"),

  sidebarPanel(textInput("term", "Enter a term", ""),
  sliderInput("cant", "Select a number of tweets",min=5,max=1500, value = 5),
  radioButtons("lang", "Select the language", c(
    "English"="en",
    "Spanish"="es",
    "Dutch"="nl")),
  submitButton(text = "Run"),

  downloadButton("download", "Download File")),

  mainPanel(
    h4("Last 5 tweets"),
    tableOutput("table"),
    plotOutput("wordcl"))
))

library(shiny)
library(twitteR)
library(wordcloud)
library(tm)

consumerKey = "My Key"
consumerSecret = "My Secret"
accessToken = "My Token"
accessSecret = "My Secret"
my_oauth <- setup_twitter_oauth(consumer_key = consumerKey, consumer_secret = consumerSecret,
                                access_token = accessToken, access_secret = accessSecret)

shinyServer(function(input,output){

  rawData <- (function(){
    tweets <- searchTwitter(input$term, n=input$cant,lang=input$lang)
    twListToDF(tweets)
  })

  output$table <- renderTable(function(){
    head(rawData()[1],n=5)
  })

output$wordcl <- renderPlot(function(){
  tw.text <- enc2native(rawData()$text)
  tw.text <- tolower(tw.text)
  tw.text <- removeWords(tw.text,c(stopwords(input$lang),"rt"))
tw.text <- removePunctuation(tw.text, TRUE)
tw.text <- unlist(strsplit(tw.text,""))

word <- sort(table(tw.text),TRUE)
wordc <- head(word,n=15)

wordcloud(names(wordc),wordc,random.color = TRUE,colors = rainbow(10),scale = c(15,2))
  })

output$download <- downloadHandler(filename = function() {paste(input$term, '.csv', sep='')},
                                   content = function(file){
                                     write.csv(rawData(), file)
                                   }
)

})

For the above code, I am getting the following output:

 <http://i.stack.imgur.com/qSHIm.png>

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

diet.graph_per.capita<- function(x){
total<- history.predict[history.predict$CityCode %in% x,]
total$Year<- as.numeric(total$Year)
capita<-ggplot(total, aes(x=Year, y=Total_Value, shape=Model, colour=Model_Class)) +
    geom_point(size=4)+
    labs(x = "Year",
         y = "Total Value (day)",
        title = paste("Total Value of City", x))+
        labs(colour="Scenario", shape= "Source")+
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = (seq(1965, 2100, by = 15)))
print(capita)
}

Is it possible that the html output has an interactive input value (that maps to the CityCode, or x input in function(x)), where whatever the selected CityCode is changed a graph is updated in the webpage? I hope this question is not extremely obvious, but if it is, or if I am missing an obvious structure, please redirect me :D
Thanks all!

Version of Shiny Server:

shiny-server --version
Shiny Server v1.4.0.721
Node.js v0.10.21

Shiny Server config file:

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as timonh;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}

messages.body_plain:

However in the case where you're absolutely certain a header can be trusted, there is a configuration option in Shiny Server Pro (only) that will let you allow whitelists of headers to make them available in Shiny: https://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#proxied-headers

Andrew,

I am sure you have seen this article on how to run RStudio Server with proxy (linking it here just in case):

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200552326-Running-with-a-Proxy

And your setup seems to be working in general. The issue is that you need some additional configuration to redirect websocket calls. This is a configuratin that works with Apache web server:

```
ProxyPassMatch ^/p/([0-9]+)/websocket/$ ws://localhost:8787/p/$1/websocket/
ProxyPass / http://localhost:8787/
ProxyPassReverse /http://localhost:8787/
ProxyRequests Off
```

The first line is needed for Shiny applications (runApp) to work within a proxy environment. You would need a similar configuration with Nginx. (I am not very familiar with Nginx syntax, but I am sure you can figure that out.)

The other thing is that depending on the Linux system you are using, you might need to enable some additional modules for websocket. For example on CentOS 7 you would need this module: proxy_wstunnel

Hope this helps,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: ProjectTemplate and Shiny (deployment)
messages.subject_clean: ProjectTemplate and Shiny (deployment)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!

I am wondering whether I can develop a Shiny app within a broader project context (i.e. a multi-level/-folder project hierarchy) and use selected resources from that project for the Shiny app.

In my particular case, I have just started working on a first small project to develop a bit of a routine in working with R. I came across ProjectTemplate (http://projecttemplate.net/) and used it to set up my project and distribute files across its suggested hierarchy (see it here http://projecttemplate.net/getting_started.html).

After getting the basics of my analysis to work, I decided to also build a Shiny app for my analysis. I placed it in src/shiny as a single app.R file. Seeing how I had developed my data processing in other files before, I started including bits of my previous work via source("../../munge/xyz.R")and the like.

Now it seems to me that this will not really work when I try to deploy either just my app.R file or the whole project hierarchy via shinyapps::deployApp().

Is it at all possible to build Shiny apps based on such a project structure and deploy them from within it? Or do I always have to copy any processing I have previously developed manually (and then keep it in sync) when I want to publish it as a Shiny app?

Best
Matt

P.S.: This seems to go in a similar direction as Nicola's question here: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/ibAXs3zLWAs/-S1_OZIDEwAJ

messages.subject: Pagination in shiny
messages.subject_clean: Pagination in shiny
messages.body_plain:
SCENARIO:

I have pagination working in my shiny app using Data Tables. The data set I am dealing with is very large and its bringing the entire records to the table which is causing me memory issues. So I decided to set "paging = FALSE" and to bring up my own action button (NEXT) to fetch the next set of records from database. (For eg: First I am bringing only 50 records from database to the table and when I click NEXT It fetches next 50 records from the database to the table, so I can avoid memory issues since only 50 records is being loaded from database each time).

There is a feature in data table for sorting columns in ascending or descending order on the click of the arrow associated with that column.

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-X4UscHcxfhs/VdNuwTuFtPI/AAAAAAAAAD4/Ga9LhDdmR0U/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2015-08-18%2Bat%2B1.43.10%2BPM.png>

With my logic right now this feature will sort only the 50 records that are fetched from the database at that time.

My question is,
So can I get the action in the click on these up and down arrow on each column so that I can write my own logic in server side in fetching the rows that are sorted (ascending/descending) based on that column from the database.

Or are there any other workarounds to achieve my scenario without bringing the entire records to the datatable?

Any help would be appreciated.

Since you're using a package, another option is to have an environment in your package for holding global-like variables that are scoped to your package. For example:

values <- new.env(parent=emptyenv())

Then when you launch shiny:

values$foo <- X
on.exit(values$foo <- NULL, add=TRUE)
shiny::runApp(...)

And in your app reference mypackage:::values$foo.

messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server currently drops cookies and all but a few HTTP headers. However, with Shiny Server Pro you can pass this data using HTTP headers with http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#proxied-headers, as long as you make sure that Apache *always* either sets or clears that header for *every* request that is sent to Shiny Server.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

After upgrading to shiny 0.12.2 I started having the following issue. In my code, I have a list of selectInput menus number of which depends on the input. All the created selectInput-s are combined in the list in a renderUI output. This produces the given number of selectInput menus in the UI. However, now every menu started to be preceded by the text 'div form-group shiny-input-container '. Setting the selectize parameter to FALSE does not help.

I would greatly appreciate giving me a hint!

Screenshot:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-v2EBQdWVvyo/VdTY45X8fzI/AAAAAAAAACo/KZuZjpnjkV4/s1600/Screenshot%2Bfrom%2B2015-08-19%2B21%253A28%253A17.png>

Fragment of code:

  output$feeding_types<-renderUI({
    if (is.null(input$taxtax)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    progress <- shiny::Progress$new()
    on.exit(progress$close())

    progress$set(message = 'Extracting feeding types',
                 detail = 'Please wait...')

    for (i in 1:10) {
      progress$set(value = i)
      Sys.sleep(0.01)
    }

    tax<-read.xls(input$taxtax$datapath,check.names=F)
    tax[,-(1:2)]<-sapply(tax[,-(1:2)],as.character)
    tax[,-(1:2)]<-sapply(tax[,-(1:2)],as.numeric)
    names(tax)[1]<-"a"
    names(tax)[2]<-"b"

    dup<-which(duplicated(names(tax))==T)

    dupl<-length(dup)

    namesl<-length(names(tax))

    if (dupl>0) {
      duplindicator<-1
      megadupset<-vector()
      for (i in 1:dupl) {
        dupset<-which(names(tax)[1:namesl]==names(tax)[dup[i]])
        megadupset<-append(megadupset,dupset)
        dupsum<-rowSums(tax[dupset])
        dupname<-names(tax)[dupset][1]
        dupsum<-cbind(dupsum)
        colnames(dupsum)<-dupname
        tax<-cbind(tax,dupsum)
      }

      tax<-tax[-megadupset]

      del<-grep(".",names(tax),fixed=T)

      if (length(del)>0) {
        tax<-tax[-del]
      }
    }

    tax<-tax[,-1]
    dat<-read.xls("database.xls")
    if (is.null(input$additem)==F){
      datadditem<-data.frame(input$additem[-1,])
      names(datadditem)<-names(dat)
      dat<-rbind(dat,datadditem)
      dat<-dat[order(as.character(dat[,1])),]
      dat[,2]<-as.integer(dat[,2])
      dat[,3]<-as.integer(dat[,3])
      dat[,4]<-as.numeric(dat[,4])
    }

    taxa<-tax[,-1]

    c<-ncol(taxa)
    i<-1
    found<-vector()
    guess<-vector()

    for (i in 1:c)
    {
      taxon<-names(taxa)[i]
      i<-i+1
      feed<-dat[dat["taxon"]==taxon][3]
      if (is.na <http://is.na>(feed)==TRUE) {
        found.value<-taxon
        found<-append(found,found.value)
      }
    }

    if (length(found)==0) {

      c<-ncol(taxa)
      i<-1
      feedvector<-vector()

      for (i in 1:c)
      {
        taxon<-names(taxa)[i]
        if (dat[dat["taxon"]==taxon][5]=="") {
          feed<-dat[dat["taxon"]==taxon][3]
        } else {
          feed<-paste(dat[dat["taxon"]==taxon][3],dat[dat["taxon"]==taxon][5],sep="")
        }
        feedvector<-append(feedvector,feed)
        i<-i+1
      }

      # sorting
      sort<-order(substr(feedvector,1,1),names(taxa))

      i<-1
      for (i in 1:c) {
        if (feedvector[i]==1) feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1a") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - sedentary parasites"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1b") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - migratory endoparasites"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1c") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - semi-endoparasites"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1d") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - ectoparasites"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1e") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - epidermal/root hair feeders"
        if (feedvector[i]=="1f") feedvector[i]<-"Herbivores - algal/lichen/moss feeders"
        if (feedvector[i]==2) feedvector[i]<-"Fungivores"
        if (feedvector[i]==3) feedvector[i]<-"Bacterivores"
        if (feedvector[i]==5) feedvector[i]<-"Predators"
        if (feedvector[i]==7) feedvector[i]<-"Animal parasites (dispersal stages)"
        if (feedvector[i]==8) feedvector[i]<-"Omnivores"
      }

      x<-length(feedvector)
      outputlist<-list()
      i<-1

      for (i in sort) {
        output<-selectInput(paste("feed",i,sep=""), colnames(taxa)[i],
                            c("Herbivores - sedentary parasites"="1a","Herbivores - migratory endoparasites"="1b","Herbivores - semi-endoparasites"="1c","Herbivores - ectoparasites"="1d","Herbivores - epidermal/root hair feeders"="1e","Herbivores - algal/lichen/moss feeders"="1f","Fungivores"=2,"Bacterivores"=3,"Predators"=5,"Animal parasites (dispersal stages)"=7,"Omnivores"=8),
                            selected=feedvector[i])
        outputlist<-append(outputlist,output)
      }

      outputlist

    } else {return(NULL)}

  })

messages.body_plain:
Yihui-

I was looking into this document http://rstudio.github.io/DT/shiny.html
There is a way to get the column selected in the data table by giving "input$tableId_columns_selected" and to get the cell selected and couple of others.
Is there a way to get the 'q$order' and 'q$columns' values from the 'dataTablesFilter' function just like this way?

On Tuesday, August 18, 2015 at 3:31:19 PM UTC-4, Yihui Xie wrote:

> Yes, it is possible to customize the server logic. See the
> documentation ?DT::dataTableAjax (in particular, the 'filter'
> argument). To understand the default server-side processing in DT, you
> may need to take a look at the source code:
> https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/master/R/shiny.R
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
>
> On Tue, Aug 18, 2015 at 1:41 PM, gerg <george...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > SCENARIO:
> >
> > I have pagination working in my shiny app using Data Tables. The data set I am dealing with is very large and its bringing the entire records to the table which is causing me memory issues. So I decided to set "paging = FALSE" and to bring up my own action button (NEXT) to fetch the next set of records from database. (For eg: First I am bringing only 50 records from database to the table and when I click NEXT It fetches next 50 records from the database to the table, so I can avoid memory issues since only 50 records is being loaded from database each time).
> >
> > There is a feature in data table for sorting columns in ascending or descending order on the click of the arrow associated with that column.
> >
> >
> >
> > With my logic right now this feature will sort only the 50 records that are fetched from the database at that time.
> >
> > My question is,
> > So can I get the action in the click on these up and down arrow on each column so that I can write my own logic in server side in fetching the rows that are sorted (ascending/descending) based on that column from the database.
> >
> > Or are there any other workarounds to achieve my scenario without bringing the entire records to the datatable?
> >
> > Any help would be appreciated.

messages.subject: Looking for technique to prevent file collision / corruption.
messages.subject_clean: Looking for technique to prevent file collision / corruption.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am developing a shiny app that will be hosted on a shiny server.  The app reads and writes multiple files.  What technique can I use to prevent file collision / corruption when multiple users use the app at the same time?  I was thinking of adding "sessionID" to part of a filename, but sessionID is not available with shiny server.

Many thanks for any help.

messages.subject: Re: Looking for technique to prevent file collision / corruption.
messages.subject_clean: Looking for technique to prevent file collision / corruption.
messages.body_plain:
Are these just temporary files or do they need to persist? If temporary, you could create a temp directory for each session under tempdir() with some random numbers added, e.g.:

file.path(tempdir(), paste0("mydata", as.integer(runif(1, min=1000000, max=9999999))))

But don't forget to delete each session's directory when the session ends (session$onSessionEnded(function() { unlink(...) }) ).

Alternatively, perhaps a proper database would make sense?

messages.subject: Re: collapsible panels in shinyBS conflicting with bootstrap.css
messages.subject_clean: collapsible panels in shinyBS conflicting with bootstrap.css
messages.body_plain:
I found the solution! At least for my case! In the bootstrap.css file, the lines:

.modal-backdrop {
  position: fixed;
  top: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 1040;
  background-color: #000000;
}

Changes to:

.modal-backdrop {
  position: fixed;
  top: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  -z-index: 1040;
  background-color: #000000;
}

The problem is in the z-index. Disable this line works like a charm!

Att,

Filipe de Morais C. Pessoa

Coordenação Geral de Planejamento - CGPL

messages.subject: How to take the value of Radio button to draw a specific ggvis plot?
messages.subject_clean: How to take the value of Radio button to draw a specific ggvis plot?
messages.body_plain:
I have this shiny app where I am taking inputs from the user and depending on the type of plot the user wants it will show that plot. But I am unable to take the value of the radio button on the app and use it to draw a specific ggvis plot because the "input$ " value can only be used within a render* function which I am not using here because I am drawing with ggvis.

My ui.R file -

library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("Xvar", "Choose X variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[2]] ),
      selectInput("Yvar", "Choose Y variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[3]] ),
      selectInput("IDvar", "Choose ID variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[4]] ),
      uiOutput("choose_COVvar"),
      uiOutput("choose_COVn"),
      br()
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(type = "tabs",
                  tabPanel("Data Exploration",
                           uiOutput("plot_type"),
                           br(),
                           ggvisOutput("ggvis_xy_plot")),
                           ggvisOutput("ggvis_profile_plot")
      )
    )
  )
))

server.R file -
library(ggvis)
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  the.data <<- mtcars

  output$plot_type <- renderUI({
    fluidRow(
      column(4, offset = 1,
             radioButtons("PlotMethod", h5("Plot type"), c("XY Scatter plot",
                                                           "profile plot"))
      )
    )
  })

  flex.data <- reactive({
    x.name <- input$Xvar
    y.name <- input$Yvar
    id.name <- input$IDvar

    x.data <- the.data[, x.name]
    y.data <- the.data[, y.name]
    ID.t <- the.data[, id.name]
    new.data <- data.frame(x.data, y.data, ID.t)
  })

  lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:nrow(flex.data()), "red")

  flex.data %>%
    ggvis(~x.data, ~y.data) %>%
    layer_points(fill := lb$fill, fill.brush := "red") %>%
    lb$input()  %>%
    layer_points(fill := "red", data = reactive(flex.data()[flex.data()$ID.t %in%
                                                              flex.data()[lb$selected(), ]$ID.t, ])) %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis_xy_plot")

  flex.data %>%
    ggvis(~x.data, ~y.data) %>%
    layer_points() %>%
    layer_lines() %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis_profile_plot")
})

As you can see, currently both the scatter plot and the line plot is there but I want it to be just one depending on the radio button above, the user has pressed.

Any help will be greatly appreciated. Thanks

Has this option been removed?

Thanks,

Fong

messages.subject: connection pooling with MonetDB, R and Shiny Pro
messages.subject_clean: connection pooling with MonetDB, R and Shiny Pro
messages.body_plain:
With R and Shiny Pro it is possible to implement multi-user analytical applications.

When a database is used to store intermediate data, how to give access to multiple user access to the db becomes very relevant and necessary.

Currently I'm using MonetDB / MonetDB.R configured (as usual for R) as a single user access, which means that any user operation occurs in sequence (users suddenly see that the app is not responsive and don't have a way to know why: e.g. the progress bar is user dependent.

I would like to implement some type of connection pooling with the DB.

>From past SO responses <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/22155727/how-to-use-connection-pooling-for-monetdb> the driver does not include connection pooling.

Are there alternatives within these toolsets?

I am starting to wonder if there is ANY similar connection-pooling implemented in any DB driver in R.  This could limit the kind of analytical apps that can be developed with R and Shiny...

Any suggestion is welcome.

(I posted this question in SO as well here http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32157446/connection-pooling-with-monetdb-r-and-shiny-pro)

messages.subject: Re: Passing arguments to reactive functions
messages.subject_clean: Passing arguments to reactive functions
messages.body_plain:
You can't pass an argument to a reactive expression. They're not called reactive functions and this is part of the reason why. Think of reactive expressions more like a variable that we are automatically keeping up-to-date for you (using the code you provided us), than like a function that executes code when you ask it.

For this particular example, I'd create two separate reactives:

get_summary_data <- function(pivot_flag = FALSE) {

      # calculate stuff
      # if !pivot_flag: select only the first two variables from raw data
      # else: select all of them
      # calculate stuff, aggregate into summary_data

      summary_data
    }

summary_data <- reactive(get_summary_data(FALSE))
summary_data_pivot <- reactive(get_summary_data(TRUE))

messages.body_plain:
The DT default is to put the whole data in memory, but that does not
have to be the case if you customize the filter function. For example,
you may just pass an empty skeleton of the data to DT::datatable()
(which consumes negligible memory), but in the filter function, you
may do SQL queries on a certain database, and that is when the page of
data is really loaded into R. You have all the query variables from
DataTables such as length and page numbers. I'm not sure if I made it
clear enough this time.

Regards,
Yihui

You might need to restart R before you install any packages on
Windows. Actually RStudio will automatically restart R when you click
the Update button in the Packages pane if the packages that you are
trying to install have already been loaded into R.

The other think to check is how many libraries you have, e.g.

  sapply(.libPaths(), list.files)

Make sure shiny is only installed in one library. It may also be
relevant which CRAN mirror you use (when in doubt, use the RStudio
mirror :).

  })

    df[!vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]

Hi Brandon -

I think the issue is that at the end of the code in renderPlot(), you call print(f). The renderPlot() code actually needs to return the plot object for interactive graphics to work properly, so you should just end the code with f, instead of print(f).

We'll try to make that clearer in the documentation.

-Winston

See Section 2 at http://rstudio.github.io/DT/server.html for an
example of what I meant by a skeleton of the data. Basically it is a
zero-row data frame with a few columns. The columns of the data frame
should match what you expect to return from the DataTables query.

That example was based on PHP. For R, your dataTablesFilterCustom is
completely up to you -- it is just a function with two arguments, and
you can do whatever you want inside the function, e.g. (pseudo code)

dataTableAjax(... filter = function(data, params) {
  # the data argument in this case may be meaningless
  list(
    draw = ...,
    data = sqlFetch("select whatever from database where this like
that limit 0,10"),
    ....
  )
})

Please take a look at the dataTablesFiler() function in DT:
https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/master/R/shiny.R

Regards,
Yihui

whatever files you want to read, e.g. read.csv for CSV, and readRDS

Hello Shiny Happy People!

I am working on a system that does not support X11, which is causing some issues with a newer versions of Shiny.

I have an app that works great R 2.15.1 and Shiny 0.10.0, but I get an X11 error when I run the same app on R 3.2.0 and Shiny 0.12.2.9000.  Some session information can be found below:

Successful:
> sessionInfo()
Oracle Distribution of R version 2.15.1  (--)

other attached packages:
 [1] shiny_0.10.0

X11 error:
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.2.0 (2015-04-16)

other attached packages:
 [1] shiny_0.12.2.9000

My suspicion is that this has to do with hovering functionality that was built into newer versions of Shiny, but I haven't been able to pinpoint exactly what about the plotOutput() is creating the X11 error.

Could anybody shed some light on what exactly is causing this issue in newer versions of Shiny and a possible way around this problem?  One idea I had was to change the Shiny app to 1) output a bitmap/pdf file instead of a renderPlot() object and 2) read this file using img() rather than plotOutput(), but I would be surprised if there isn't a more elegant way to address this issue.

Thanks!

- Derek

messages.body_plain:
My gut feeling is that there is something wrong with your R
installation. In particular, you may have built R from source but did
not install the cairo/pango libraries properly. I think the error
message about X11 is fairly misleading (we have seen it many times in
this mailing list). It basically means the default setting for png()
does not work (see the `type` argument), and R falls back to X11. If
you use Debian/Ubuntu, you need to run apt-get build-dep r-base-dev to
install all the dependencies before you build R from source.

Regards,
Yihui

But the resulting plot rounds the fractional x values to whole seconds. I found the following two links to show how to handle milliseconds.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31299871/dygraph-millisecond-plotting
https://github.com/rstudio/dygraphs/issues/46

library(dygraphs)

                              return Dygraph.zeropad(d.getHours()) + ":" +

                                     Dygraph.zeropad(d.getMilliseconds());

messages.subject: Re: Getting Shiny to work with apache passthrough
messages.subject_clean: Getting Shiny to work with apache passthrough
messages.body_plain:
Ok, After much trial and tribulation, I've found the solution. The shiny-server.conf file is correct. However, for Apache in Ubuntu2 , you need to add a file (in my case I called it RshinyPass.conf) to /etc/apache2/sites-available. In it, put:

        Redirect /yourappname /yourappname/
        ProxyPass /yourappname/ http://127.0.0.1:3838/yourappname/ <http://127.0.0.1:3838/yourappname/>
        ProxyPassReverse /yourappname/ http://127.0.0.1:3838/yourappname/ <http://127.0.0.1:3838/yourappname/>

Then do sudo a2ensite RshinyPass.conf
Then sudo service apache2 reload
Then sudo service apache2 restart (for good measure) :-).

Be sure to disable the default 000-default.conf

messages.subject: Building a datatable using input values bound by Shiny.bindAll
messages.subject_clean: Building a datatable using input values bound by Shiny.bindAll
messages.body_plain:
I have created a datatable which has selectInput widgets in one of the columns. Another column of the datatable should take inputs given in the first column, and use them to look up a number from my data source. The inputs are binding correctly in Shiny, by using preDrawCallback and drawCallback functions, but lookup values are not updating when the inputs change. Strangely, they do update when I do the lookup in a separate data table. A reproducible example is here:

    library(shiny)
    library(DT)

    data <- data.frame(c(1:7),c(21:27))

    shinyApp(
      server = shinyServer(function(input, output) {
          output$table <- DT::renderDataTable({

            Rows <- c(1:7)
            temp <- data.frame(Rows)
            temp[,"Item"] <- ""
            temp[,"Value"] <- ""
            temp$Rows <- NULL

            sapply(1:7, FUN = function(i) {
              temp$Item[i] <<- as.character(selectInput(paste("Item.1.1",i, sep = "."), "",
                                                           choices = setNames(c(1:7),c(1:7)),
                                                           selected = 1,
                                                           multiple = FALSE))
            })

             sapply(1:7, FUN = function(i) {
               temp$Value[i] <<- data[eval(parse(text = paste("input$Item.1.1",i, sep = "."))),2]
             })

            datatable(temp, escape = FALSE, rownames = FALSE,
                      options = list(sort = FALSE, paging = FALSE, searching = FALSE, dom = 't',
                                     columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center', targets = 0:1)),
                                     preDrawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node()); }'),
                                     drawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node()); } ')
                      ))
        }, server = FALSE)
      }),
      ui = fluidPage(
        dataTableOutput("table")
      )
    )

That gives the error "Error in temp$Value[i] <<- data[eval(parse(text = paste("input$Item.1.1",  :
  replacement has length zero".

My best guess is that unbindAll is clearing out all of my input$Item values before the Value column is created, but bindAll isn't taking affect until after trying to create Value.

Regardless of whether my guess is right, I much appreciate any help that can be offered.

P.S. I have tried creating a second datatable, which is built from the Input$Item's, and it seems to update fine---provided I comment out the code that builds my Value column. Things are *much* simplified for my user when I can have them all in the same datatable, so I really don't want to have to do this if it can be avoided. I'll provide this half-working example in another post following shortly.
